title: Grateful Dead Live at The Spectrum on 1982-04-06
lineage: Dat -> Samplitude Professional v10.22 -> Adobe Audition v1.5 -> FLAC/16

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy spring ’82 show, highlighted by a smoking Shakedown Street opener and an intense Other One → Morning Dew sequence.
ai_review.review: The Miller SBD delivers a buttery, fat mix that puts Phil’s bass front‑and‑center and lets Jerry’s guitar blaze through the set. The performance is tight and exuberant, with standout moments like Shakedown Street, Candyman, Jack‑A‑Roe and an electrifying Other One into Morning Dew, while the second set maintains a high‑octane flow throughout.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating is ~4.37/5 across 19 reviews, overwhelmingly positive about both music and sound quality; ample detailed comments give strong confidence.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Smooth, buttery mix with full, wide stereo image; Phil’s bass is prominent and funky. No major flaws reported – reviewers note it as the best or an excellent SBD of early ’82, with only occasional mentions of minor drop‑outs in other releases (not this Miller source).

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set builds warm and tight, leading into a powerhouse second set that rides high energy with seamless transitions, especially the Shakedown opener and the intense Other One/Morning Dew climax.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised as 'on fire', delivering perfect tone and inspiring solos; key driver of the show’s intensity.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for a prominent, funky bass presence in the mix – “much more prevalent” than earlier years.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent (and Bobby) highlighted for lively interplay with Jerry; keyboards described as solid though not overly hot.
band_member_comments.Drums: Described as solid and dynamic, especially during the second‑set drum segment.
